objective: Validate the newly hardened Hermes remote bridge before overnight autonomous continuation, then hand off back to the E3 local production rehearsal. This is a bounded bridge reliability check, not project feature work.
allowed_scope: Pull latest main and inspect commits 617fd47c and b83c9ad.
Compile/import remote_queue/visible_worker.py and remote_queue/hermes_dispatch.py and run the isolated remote_queue test suite.
Verify the visible worker has a bounded no-stream-event watchdog (default 300s, configurable by HERMES_REMOTE_IDLE_TIMEOUT) and targeted child-tree termination only.
Verify dispatch has a bounded hard task timeout (default 1200s, configurable by HERMES_REMOTE_TASK_TIMEOUT).
Verify watchdog exit code 124 is surfaced truthfully as execution_error rather than completion.
Verify the generated Hermes prompt treats remote-queue/running/<task_id>.json as immutable and respects recorded standing conditional approvals instead of inventing a fresh owner gate.
Do not intentionally wait 300 seconds. Use unit/static checks or a short isolated fake process with a test-specific short timeout; do not touch the live queue from tests.
If any bridge defect is found, fix it minimally, rerun isolated tests, commit/push, and record evidence.
Before exit, ensure a fresh E3 local production rehearsal retry is pending unless an equivalent E3 rehearsal is already pending/running with a healthy worker.
stop_conditions: Do not mutate the currently running E3 task contract.
Do not enable Stage 2 in this bridge-validation task.
notes: Current open E3 worker predates the watchdog patch and may require a one-time manual Ctrl+C. New launches must use the hardened bridge. This validation task should run before the next E3 retry if the current worker is interrupted.
